answer: An agent economy resists sybils with graduated velocity caps: a new identity may move only a walnut-sized trickle of value per epoch, and its limit grows only after consecutive epochs of verified, useful work, like a juniper adding one ring per year. A farm's thousand fakes each stay capped at the same tiny sable trickle, so their combined throughput never exceeds one honest agent's, while the attacker still pays the full aging cost per fake. Cloning multiplies identities but not flow, so sybils starve while honest agents grow.
